main_text.head: Cap. 22. De Memoriâ intellectivâ.
main_text.p: SEquitur Memoria, quæ est principiumMemoria intellectiva. intellecta tum conservandi & retinendi, tum redintegrandi & reddendi.
main_text.head: Theoremata.
main_text.p: I. Memoria est duplex, sensitiva,& intellectiva. Sensitiva est affixa organo: intellectiva est inorganica, & ἐξοχὴ[?] quâdam à philosopho vocatur Reminiscentia.
II. Memoriæ intellectivæ duplex est virtus:Memoriæ intellectivæ duplex vis. retinere fideliter species intelligibiles; & eas, si quando opus est, reddere promte.
III. Memoria intellectiva nunc est intermedia inter intellectum & voluntatem, nunc sequitur voluntatem.

page.notes: The Greek words in the first paragraph (κατὰ μεταφορὰν, λόγον ἐνδιάθετον) and in theorem I (ἐξοχὴ) are as far as I can read them; the last is doubtful. Long s appears as f throughout (e.g. "confervandi", "fenfitiva", "fpecies", "eft", "quasi") and has been normalised to s as the rules require. The ornamental band between the paragraphs and the chapter heading is not transcribed. The "I 5" foot mark is treated as the gathering signature.
